title: textContent, safe DOM construction, sanitization concepts
learningObjectives: Explain textcontent, safe dom construction, sanitization concepts and apply secure, accessible, maintainable browser practices.

understand.concept: textContent inserts text without parsing markup. createElement and append build DOM nodes safely when values are assigned as text. If rich user-authored HTML is a genuine requirement, use a maintained sanitizer with a strict allowlist and safe URL handling.
understand.whyItMatters: Sanitization is context-specific and easy to get wrong when implemented manually. Prefer avoiding HTML parsing entirely for ordinary text and use established sanitization libraries for rich content.
understand.analogy: Safe DOM construction assembles real elements from trusted structure and inserts user values only as text.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser security, accessibility, and performance rules depend on platform behaviour and server configuration.

explain.narrative: The element structure is created by code and the title is assigned as text, so it is not parsed as markup.

examples.explanation: The element structure is created by code and the title is assigned as text, so it is not parsed as markup.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the security or reliability principle.

practise.guidedTask: Build a comment renderer with createElement and textContent. Document the strict sanitizer policy needed if formatted HTML must be supported.
practise.independentTask: Review a small browser feature for security, accessibility, performance, and lifecycle risks. Add a fallback and document the server-side controls required.
hints: Treat all browser and network input as untrusted.
Use exact origin checks and least privilege.
Measure performance and clean up resources.

questions.prompt: Which approach avoids parsing an untrusted string as HTML?
questions.explanation: Construct trusted elements and assign untrusted values as text.

questions.prompt: What is a sound browser engineering principle?
options: Defence in depth, least privilege, and usable fallbacks
Assume all browser features are always available
questions.answer: Defence in depth, least privilege, and usable fallbacks
questions.explanation: Secure and reliable interfaces combine trusted server enforcement with careful client behaviour.
